title: 1 Cor 6:11: justified with washed and sanctified—real change
source_text: IX. Similiter putant viri illi Docti justificationem non designare solam a peccati poenis absolutionem, sed realem in nobis abolitionem, veramque nostri immutationem & innovationem, 1. Cor. 6. Et haec quidem fuistis, scil. avari, ebriosi, rapaces, maledici, fornicarii; sed abluti estis, sed sanctificati estis, sed justificati estis, in nomine Domini Jesu, & in Spiritu Dei nostri. Paulus enim ibi tribuit justificationem nostram Spiritui Sancto, cujus proprium est nos interius innovare. Deinde manifestum est per justificationem Paulum significare mutationem aliquam, per quam Corinthii cessaverunt esse id quod antea erant, nempe fornicarii, ebriosi, &c. quales regnum Dei possidere non possunt. Per solam autem a peccati poenis absolutionem, non desinit aliquis his vitiis infectus esse, sed per internam Spiritus Sancti renovationem. Adde quod, si justificati non aliud ibi significat quam a peccati poenis absoluti, frigida & diluta erit oratio Pauli, qui postquam dixit quod magis est, quasi tamen exaggerans subjungit id quod minus. Plus enim est abluti, quam simpliciter a poena absoluti: nam ablutio praeter condonationem poenae, includit veram a peccati sordibus purgationem.
pass_a_gloss: Likewise those learned men think that justification does not designate mere absolution from the penalties of sin, but a real abolition in us, and a true change and renewal of ourselves, 1 Cor. 6. And such indeed you were—greedy, drunkards, rapacious, revilers, fornicators; but you were washed, but you were sanctified, but you were justified, in the name of the Lord Jesus, and in the Spirit of our God. For Paul there attributes our justification to the Holy Spirit, whose proper work is to renew us inwardly. Next it is manifest that by justification Paul signifies some change by which the Corinthians ceased to be what they were before—namely fornicators, drunkards, etc., such as cannot possess the kingdom of God. But by mere absolution from the penalties of sin someone does not cease to be infected with these vices, but by the inward renewal of the Holy Spirit. Add that if justified there signifies nothing else than absolved from the penalties of sin, Paul's speech will be cold and diluted, who after he has said what is greater, as if exaggerating, subjoins what is less. For it is more to be washed than simply to be absolved from penalty: for washing, besides the condonation of penalty, includes a true cleansing from the filth of sin.
pass_b_english: 1 Cor 6:11: justified listed with washed and sanctified—Spirit renews inwardly.
Bare penalty-acquittal would anticlimax after washed; washing includes real cleansing.

choices.why: Paired with abluti/sanctificati as real change.
